q: How does a water utility calculate CO2 per kL supplied?
title: Water utility CO2 per kL supplied
short: Add pumping and treatment electricity, multiply by 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, then divide by kL supplied. State whether you divide by water pumped or water billed: leaks and other non revenue water raise the figure per billed kL.
audience: Municipal water utilities and industrial estates supplying water

ul: Pump station and treatment plant meters.

p: Fixing leaks lowers emissions per billed kL even when the pumps run the same hours.

example.title: Worked example (illustrative figures)
lines: Pumping and treatment: 400,000 kWh × 0.710 = 284,000 kg CO2.
Water pumped: 1,000,000 kL, so 0.284 kg per kL pumped.
Water billed: 700,000 kL, so 0.406 kg per kL billed.

senseible: Senseible reads electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and diesel, LPG and gas invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a dated, fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record for each site. Intensity per unit uses the activity count you enter, and estimates are labelled as estimates.
